title: Sending Information with Patterns
seo_title: Grade 4 Codes and Patterns Worksheets: Morse Code, Light Signals and Sending Information
standard_text: Generate and compare multiple solutions that use patterns to transfer information.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 science worksheets on sending information with patterns (NGSS 4-PS4-3): Morse code with a key, light and on-off codes, and comparing ways to send messages using criteria. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Patterns can carry information over a distance.
key_sub: A code is a set of patterns that the sender and receiver both understand, like Morse code or on-off lights.
body_html:
How to think about it

People can send information over a distance using patterns. A code is a set of patterns with meanings that the sender and receiver both know.

  • Morse code: short signals (•) and long signals (—) stand for letters. They can be sent as beeps, flashes or taps.
  • Lights and flags: each pattern or color means something, like a traffic light.
  • Computers and phones: send information as patterns of on and off, written as 1s and 0s.

To choose the best way, compare solutions using criteria: How far must the message go? Is it dark or noisy? How fast must it arrive?

Example

With the key • — = A and — • = N, what does “• — / — •” spell?

• — is A.

— • is N.

Answer: AN

Example

Which signal works best in a noisy gym?

Sound is hard to hear in noise.

Light can still be seen.

Answer: a flashing light or hand signal

Common mistakes

  • Reading the letters in the wrong order.
  • Choosing a light signal when there is a wall or fog in the way.
  • Choosing a sound signal in a very noisy place.

faq.a: Each pattern stands for a letter or a message. The receiver uses a key to decode it, like dots and dashes in Morse code.

faq.q: How do phones and computers send information?
faq.a: They send patterns of on and off signals, written as 1s and 0s.

faq.q: How do you choose the best way to send a message?
faq.a: Compare the solutions using criteria such as distance, speed, and whether it works in the dark or in a noisy place.

items.q: Long ago, how could people on hills send a warning to towns far away?
c: by mailing a letter that took weeks
by lighting fires or smoke signals in a pattern
items.e: Patterns of fire and smoke can be seen from far away.

items.q: A code uses a row of 5 lights. Each light can be on or off. How many different messages can it send?
items.e: Each light doubles the number of patterns: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 32.

items.q: What is the famous Morse code message for help?
items.e: SOS is three dots, three dashes, three dots.

items.q: What is a code?
c: a type of wave that carries water
a set of patterns that stand for messages or letters
items.e: In Morse code, short and long signals stand for letters.

sets.title: Choosing the best way to send a message

c: flashing a flashlight in a pattern
items.e: Flags, signs and hand signals cannot be seen in the dark.

items.q: Why do ships use flag codes during the day and light codes at night?
c: Flags can be seen in daylight, but only lights can be seen in the dark.
Lights do not work in the day.
Flags are too heavy at night.
items.e: Engineers pick a solution that fits the conditions.

items.q: Leo's code uses a long beep for every letter. Why is this a problem?
c: Every letter would look the same, so the message could not be read.
items.e: Each letter needs its own pattern.
